name: Imatinib
route_note: oral tablets once or twice daily with food
originator: Ciba-Geigy (Nicholas Lydon, Jürg Zimmermann and colleagues), with Brian Druker at Oregon Health & Science University
owner: generic (many); Gleevec/Glivec brand held by Novartis

discovery.by: Jürg Zimmermann, Nicholas Lydon, Elisabeth Buchdunger and colleagues, Ciba-Geigy; Brian Druker, OHSU
discovery.note: A 2-phenylaminopyrimidine optimised to bind the inactive conformation of the ABL kinase; Druker's laboratory showed selective killing of BCR-ABL-positive CML cells.

tagline: Landmark kinase inhibitor that turned chronic myeloid leukaemia into a manageable disease
summary: Imatinib was the first rationally designed tyrosine kinase inhibitor to transform a cancer's outlook: it blocks the BCR-ABL fusion kinase that drives chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML), giving most patients near-normal life expectancy. It also inhibits KIT and PDGFR and is standard therapy for gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST).
mechanism: The Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) fuses BCR to ABL1, producing a constitutively active tyrosine kinase that drives myeloid proliferation.

Imatinib occupies the ATP-binding pocket of ABL when the kinase is in its inactive (DFG-out) conformation, preventing substrate phosphorylation and downstream signalling, and inducing apoptosis of BCR-ABL-positive cells. Resistance commonly arises through kinase-domain mutations such as T315I.
The same mechanism inhibits KIT (mutated in most GISTs) and PDGFRA/B, explaining activity in GIST, hypereosinophilic syndromes and dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.
uses: Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukaemia (all phases)
KIT-positive gastrointestinal stromal tumours (metastatic and adjuvant)
Hypereosinophilic syndrome and chronic eosinophilic leukaemia

history.title: Philadelphia chromosome
history.detail: Peter Nowell and David Hungerford describe a small chromosome in CML cells.

history.title: Translocation
history.detail: Janet Rowley shows the Philadelphia chromosome results from a t(9;22) translocation.

history.title: Selective killing
history.detail: Druker et al. (Nature Medicine) report that CGP 57148 selectively inhibits BCR-ABL-positive cells.

history.title: Rapid FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Gleevec for CML in about 10 weeks after submission; Time magazine features it as a 'magic bullet'.

history.title: GIST
history.detail: Approved for KIT-positive gastrointestinal stromal tumours.

history.title: IRIS
history.detail: IRIS trial shows imatinib is superior to interferon plus cytarabine in newly diagnosed CML.

history.title: Indian patent ruling
history.detail: India's Supreme Court rejects Novartis's patent on the beta-crystalline form, a landmark decision on evergreening.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic imatinib launches in the US.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP3A4 to active N-desmethyl imatinib

serious: severe fluid retention and congestive heart failure

facts: Ten-year overall survival in the IRIS trial was about 83%.
The Philadelphia chromosome was the first consistent chromosomal abnormality linked to a cancer.
